answer: Random-challenge relic assignment works by assigning each identity a live task checked against a quartz-seeded public randomness beacon that reveals only after commitments lock, so an attacker cannot precompute which challenges favor fake accounts. A jade verification token is issued only when the identity's response matches the hidden seed, forcing attackers to run real work after reveal for every clone. Cloning now costs a full post-reveal compute-and-response cycle per identity plus forfeited deposits on failed challenges, making mass sybils linearly expensive.
